_comment: Kentucky FY2027 9% LIHTC scoring, Kentucky Housing Corporation. The first spreadsheet source in the corpus. Kentucky publishes no point values in any PDF: the 107-page Multifamily Guidelines reference the scoring workbook eleven times without reproducing a value, and the 2027-2029 QAP states that KHC makes awards 'without determining points'. The workbook is therefore the operative document. It is read as a document whose pages are sheets, so page_start is the sheet ordinal (sheet 3, '3)Scoring Overview'), and cell_ref names the exact cell each figure was read from. TWO PARALLEL POOLS, coded as tracks on the Michigan precedent because the same criterion carries different values in each: Urban totals 75 and Balance of State totals 75, both stated in the workbook's own Total row. Four criteria are pool-specific: Employment Density and Significant Share are Balance of State only, Road Network Density and Revitalization Plans are Urban only. A third pool, Existing Supply at roughly 10% of credits, is scored by nobody: '3)Scoring Overview'!B6 states 'This pool will have NO scoring.'

track_totals.note: Stated in '3)Scoring Overview'!H15, the Total row of the Max. Pts. Urban column. The Urban pool takes roughly 30% of overall credits per '3)Scoring Overview'!F4.

Stated in '3)Scoring Overview'!J15, the Total row of the Balance of State column. The pool takes roughly 60% of overall credits per '3)Scoring Overview'!F5. The two pools reach the same 75 by different routes: Balance of State pays more for employment density and county affordable-unit share, Urban pays more for median household income, road network density and revitalization plans.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: renter cost burdens
criteria.note: Worth 20% of the Urban total, the joint largest share alongside median household income. Measures the percentage of renters spending 30% or more of income on housing, per the narrative at '2)New Supply'!B14. The underlying data is PolicyMap's, so the test cannot be evaluated from the workbook alone. Carries the same 15 points in both pools, the only criterion that does.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: median household income
criteria.note: Measures local median income as a share of area median income, per '2)New Supply'!B19. Worth 15 in Urban against 10 in Balance of State.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: road network density
criteria.note: URBAN POOL ONLY; '3)Scoring Overview'!K10 records 0% of the Balance of State total. Measures how many roadway links run from intersections, per '2)New Supply'!B32 — a proxy for street connectivity and walkability.

criteria.heading: Permanent below market sources
criteria.note: The single largest criterion in either pool, 20 points and 26.7% of the Urban total. For permanent grants or loans at below market rate, or secured land, per '2)New Supply'!B52. The terms must carry an interest rate of no more than 4%, per '2)New Supply'!B57.

criteria.heading: Revitalization plans for QCTs
criteria.note: URBAN POOL ONLY; '3)Scoring Overview'!K13 records 0% of the Balance of State total. The smallest criterion in the workbook.

criteria.heading: Family, senior, or supportive housing
criteria.note: Ten points in both pools. The only criterion in either pool that scores who the housing is for rather than where it sits or how it is financed.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: renter cost burdens
criteria.note: The Balance of State counterpart of U.1, at the same 15 points. The criterion is named once in column G and its Balance of State value read from '3)Scoring Overview'!J7; cell_ref points at the cell holding the quoted text.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: median household income
criteria.note: Worth 10 here against 15 in the Urban pool. The criterion is named once in column G and its Balance of State value read from '3)Scoring Overview'!J8; cell_ref points at the cell holding the quoted text.

criteria.heading: PolicyMap: employment density
criteria.note: BALANCE OF STATE ONLY; '3)Scoring Overview'!I9 records 0% of the Urban total. Measures jobs per unit of area, per '2)New Supply'!B26. Its 15 points are the structural counterweight to Urban's road network density and revitalization plan points: rural applications are asked to show economic activity where urban ones are asked to show street connectivity.

criteria.heading: Significant share of county's affordable units
criteria.quote: Significant Share of County's Affordable Units
criteria.note: BALANCE OF STATE ONLY; '3)Scoring Overview'!I11 records 0% of the Urban total. For developments accounting for a significant number of the county's available affordable units, per '2)New Supply'!B40. Sheet '4)# Affordable Units' carries the county-by-county counts it is measured against, sourced from the National Housing Preservation Database and updated 27 March 2026.

criteria.heading: Permanent below market sources
criteria.note: Worth 15 here against 20 in the Urban pool, but still the joint largest Balance of State criterion. The criterion is named once in column G and its Balance of State value read from '3)Scoring Overview'!J12; cell_ref points at the cell holding the quoted text.

criteria.heading: Family, senior, or supportive housing
criteria.note: The Balance of State counterpart of U.8, at the same 10 points. The criterion is named once in column G and its Balance of State value read from '3)Scoring Overview'!J14; cell_ref points at the cell holding the quoted text.

criteria.heading: Greatest number of LIHTC units
criteria.note: Applied in listed order, per '3)Scoring Overview'!F18: 'In the event more than one application earns the same score, KHC will apply the following tiebreakers in the order listed.'

criteria.heading: Eligibility for the historic rehabilitation credit
Existing Supply pool is not scored
criteria.quote: This pool will have NO scoring.
criteria.note: Recorded so the absence is visible rather than looking like missing extraction work. The Existing Supply pool takes roughly 10% of overall credits per '3)Scoring Overview'!B3, and KHC selects within it against named criteria — greatest need of rehabilitation, project-based rent assistance, rehabilitation credits only — with no points and, per '3)Scoring Overview'!B18, no tiebreakers.
